title: ML-forecasted soft-quota admission and defer-proxy for dedicated fleets
creator: Anjali Patel
description: Introduce a machine-learning driven soft-quota admission layer plus a lightweight defer-proxy to reduce hard rejects during short bursts on Dedicated fleets. The feature dynamically assigns short-window soft quotas per tenant based on near-term demand forecasts and historical burst patterns. When a tenant exceeds its soft quota, the admission layer will: 1) transparently defer low-urgency requests into a short-lived slowpath queue with backoff hints, or 2) mark requests as deprioritized and allow best-effort execution if headroom exists. The system integrates with the autoscaler to trigger informed scale-up signals when predicted demand exceeds available capacity, and emits detailed signals to Console for visibility and billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Forecast model achieves >=0.75 weighted F1 on short-window (15m-1h) tenant demand classification in production-like workloads
Soft-quotas computed and applied per-tenant with per-tenant TTL; 95% of expected burst events are handled by defer or deprioritization rather than immediate 429 rejects
Defer-proxy yields median additional latency <= 250ms for queued-turnaround path; backpressure and TTL ensure no request waits > 30s
Autoscaler receives prediction-derived scale hints and suppresses noisy signals; false-positive scale-ups reduced by >=30% in simulated workloads
Observability: per-tenant metrics (predicted demand, soft-quota, deferred count, deprioritized count, reject rate) surfaced in Console routes dashboard
E2E integration tests and a Canary rollout plan validated in staging; rollback triggers and playbook documented
notes: 2026-01-12: Spike started to evaluate forecasting approaches (LightGBM vs simple ARIMA vs small transformer). Initial shortlist: LightGBM for tabular features + a lightweight LSTM for anomaly detection.
2026-01-25: Prototype ML model (LightGBM) trained on last 90 days of tenant p99 QPS and token distribution. Achieved 0.78 weighted F1 on 15m-window prediction task in offline test.

2026-02-02: Design review feedback (Sophie Renaud): require explicit opt-out for tenants that cannot tolerate any deferred execution; ensure telemetry tags for regulated tenants. Action: add tenant-level policy flag 'admission_fallback' and RBAC guard in Private deployments.
2026-02-14: Implemented admission shim with feature flag behind 'ml-softquota-v1'. Local integration tests for per-tenant quota enforcement passed.
2026-02-22: Built defer-proxy (lightweight in-proc queue) with TTL and exponential backoff hints to clients. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4882
2026-03-01: Autoscaler hooks added: prediction-hint endpoint and scale-confidence parameter. Need to tune suppression window to prevent thrash during oscillatory demand.
2026-03-08: Performance test in canary cluster: defer-path median turnaround 180ms, 95th 1.8s; observed 62% fewer hard 429s versus baseline under synthetic burst traffic.

Open trade-offs: model complexity vs inference cost (we prefer LightGBM for predict cost), soft-quota aggressiveness vs customer latency guarantees (we default to conservative soft limits for high-SLA tenants), and where to place the defer-proxy (edge vs fleet ingress) — current plan is fleet-ingress to preserve routing locality.
Next steps: finalize model retraining cadence, implement tenant policy UI in Console, add end-to-end billing reconciliation job, run 2-week staggered canary before GA.
